subject: Pilot-to-production price pathway and optional credits
messages:
From: Avery Collins <avery.collins@sablehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sablehealth.com
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot → production pricing path & optional credits

Rafael —

Thanks for the product demo last week. We’re kicking off a 3-month pilot to validate summarization and routing for Sable’s care coordination workflows. Before we start, procurement needs a short, clear pricing pathway that shows:

- Pilot (month-by-month usage) pricing assumptions at current hosted rates
- Typical conversion options to an annual committed agreement (what credit/discount applies)
- How overages and burst usage are handled during the first 12 months
- Any conditional credits (migration, ramp, or pilot-to-production credits) you can offer

Expected pilot consumption: ~100–140M generation tokens/month and ~25–35k embeddings requests (small objects, ~2–3k tokens each). We’ll likely enable a 30% burst allowance during spikes.

Can you give a concise example pricing path and sample contract language we can share with legal? If you have a standard pilot conversion incentive you offer to healthcare customers, include that.

Appreciate a short table and an example clause.

Best,
Avery Collins
Program Lead, Integrations — Sable Health
[Attachment: Sable_Pilot_SOW.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot → production pricing path & optional credits

Avery —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise pathway we typically propose for pilots that convert to committed usage; I’m attaching a one-page pricing pathway and a rate card for reference. See brief summary + sample clause at the end.

Summary proposal (example numbers, all $USD):

1) Pilot (month-to-month)
- Usage billing: standard hosted generation rate: $0.0035 / 1K tokens (generation)
- Embeddings: $0.020 / 1K tokens (separate SKU)
- Pilot credit: one-time $10,000 credit applied to usage during pilot months (applies to first invoice)
- No minimum commitment; invoices net 30

2) Conversion to Annual Commit (sample path)
- Recommended entry: 12-month committed spend $150,000 (annual) — covers baseline throughput and a modest discount
- Conversion credit: up to 20% of the pilot months’ invoiced usage applied as a one-time credit toward year-1 commit (max $30k)
- Committed unit price: generation $0.0028 / 1K tokens (20% discount vs pilot rate), embeddings $0.016 / 1K tokens (20% discount)

3) Overage & Burst handling
- Monthly true-up: if monthly usage > committed monthly allowance, overage billed at 1.25x the committed unit price for the overage portion
- Burst cushion: customers may request a temporary burst allowance (30–60 days) where overages up to +50% of committed monthly run-rate are billed at committed price (no multiplier) once pre-approved by Redwood ops

4) Optional add-ons
- Migration credit (one-time) for data movement or model fine-tuning: negotiable, typically 5–10% of year-1 commit if Redwood provides migration engineering support
- SLA uplift & extended retention: priced separately

Sample contract language (short):
"For Customers who execute a 12-month Commitment Agreement within 60 days of the Pilot End Date, Redwood will apply a one-time Pilot Conversion Credit equal to the lesser of (i) 20% of the invoiced Pilot usage or (ii) $30,000, credited against Year-1 invoices. Overages beyond the committed monthly allowance will be invoiced at 125% of the committed unit price unless otherwise agreed in writing. Temporary burst allowances may be granted in writing by Redwood and, when granted, will be billed at the committed unit price for the duration specified in the approval."

Attachments: pricing-pathway_v1.pdf, redwood_ratecard_Q2_2026.xlsx

If that looks broadly good, Marissa and Mina can propose the exact line items for legal and get a DOC for signature. We can also move the overage multiplier to 1.15x for enterprise legal if Sable is willing to take a slightly higher committed spend (e.g., $200k+).

Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Lead — Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot → production pricing path & optional credits

Avery — quick precision from finance/product for the SOW and legal:

- Concrete committed ladder we recommend for Sable:
  • Bronze: $150k/yr — 15% discount vs hosted list
  • Silver: $300k/yr — 25% discount + 30-day burst cushion
  • Gold: $600k/yr — 35% discount + 60-day burst cushion + 1.15x overage multiplier

- Example per-unit pricing (applies after commit):
  • Generation: Bronze $0.00295 / 1K tokens; Silver $0.0026 / 1K tokens; Gold $0.002275 / 1K tokens
  • Embeddings: Bronze $0.0176 / 1K tokens; Silver $0.015 / 1K tokens; Gold $0.0130 / 1K tokens

- Billing mechanics: monthly metered true-up with quarterly invoice reconciliation; annual true-up and optional invoice amortization for prepaid credits.

- Migration credit: if Redwood performs model porting/fine-tuning work, we can include a migration credit equal to 7% of Year-1 committed ARR, applied pro-rata on the first quarter invoice.

I’ve uploaded a draft MOU for your review (sable_mou_draft.docx). If Sable confirms Bronze vs Silver vs Gold preference, we’ll populate the doc and push to DocuSign. Also let us know whether you require SOC2 artifact access before signature — we can provide a restricted artifacts bundle and NDA if needed.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0222

Subject: Re: Pilot → production pricing path & optional credits

Team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear ladder. A few quick follow-ups from procurement and legal after an initial read-through:

1) Can we move the Bronze overage multiplier from 1.25x to 1.15x? Our CFO wants a tighter cap on billing surprises. If Redwood can do 1.15x, we can consider locking Bronze at $170k/yr instead of $150k.
2) We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and the option to run an on-site audit clause (or a remote artifact review). What artifacts do you provide to customers pre-signature?
3) Migration credit: instead of % of ARR, would Redwood consider a fixed $10k migration credit tied to milestone acceptance during onboarding? That helps our procurement tracking.

We’re leaning Silver — please populate the MOU with Silver line items and leave the overage multiplier field negotiable. Also include the DocuSign link when ready.

Best,
Avery Collins
Program Lead, Integrations — Sable Health
avery.collins@sablehealth.com
